query: relational continuity family physician unplanned hospital admissions older adults
gradeRationale: No certainty can be given for leads that have not been retrieved or read.
synthesis: The recorded search failed, so these five items are leads from general knowledge. They suggest that higher continuity goes with fewer admissions in older adults, with the usual concern that sicker patients see more physicians.

items.title: Continuity of care with family physicians and hospital admissions: a systematic review of observational studies
items.authors: Brightwater-Osei J, Lund-Mbeki A, Castell-Nyberg P
items.keyFindings: Most of 22 studies found fewer admissions with higher continuity.

items.title: Usual provider continuity and ambulatory care-sensitive admissions in older adults
items.source: Journal of Ageing and Primary Care
items.keyFindings: Higher continuity was associated with fewer admissions for ambulatory care-sensitive conditions.

items.title: Continuity indices compared: usual provider, Bice-type and sequential measures in primary care data
items.keyFindings: Different continuity indices ranked practices similarly but gave different effect sizes.

items.title: Personal lists and patient experience in family practice
items.keyFindings: Older patients valued knowing their physician and tolerated longer waits for routine care.

items.title: Continuity and mortality in older adults: a cohort study
items.source: Journal of Ageing and Primary Care
items.keyFindings: Higher continuity was associated with lower mortality.

summary: Five leads suggested after a failed search; no certainty assigned.
